newsitem.title: UK: Angerstein launches new Lloyd's investment scheme.
newsitem.headline: Angerstein launches new Lloyd's investment scheme.

text.p: Angerstein Underwriting Trust Plc on Friday unveiled a way for traditional backers of the Lloyd's insurance market to move from unlimited to limited liability.

Following record losses in the early 1990s the number of traditional, individual backers, known as Names, has fallen to 10,000 from a peak of 33,000 and many of those remaining are keen to move to limited liability status.
"We have concentrated on devising a scheme which should be attractive to Names and beneficial to the Angerstein Group,' the company said in a statement.
A spokesman said Angerstein was the first of the quoted Lloyd's spread investment companies to come up with a limited liability conversion scheme for Names.
The scheme will operate through a new corporate capital vehicle at Lloyd's, Stace Barr Angerstein Plc. Stace Barr Limited is the wholly owned members' agent of Angerstein.
Other limited liability schemes are expected to be announced in time for Names to convert from unlimited liability before the closing date for applications for the 1998 underwriting year.

Names account for 56 percent of Lloyd's 1997 10.3 billion stg underwriting capacity, with the remaining 44 percent being supplied by corporate investors who were first allowed into the market in 1994.
